overview.description: Golden Gate uses Type IIS enzymes (which cut outside their recognition site) to create scarless, directional, one-tube assemblies of 10+ fragments. Because cut sites are removed during assembly, ligation can proceed immediately - no purification step.
objectives: use Type IIS enzymes that cut outside their recognition site
design fragments without internal recognition sites ('domestication')
assemble many ordered fragments in one reaction

steps.description: Golden Gate uses Type IIS enzymes (which cut outside their recognition site) to create scarless, directional, one-tube assemblies of 10+ fragments. Because cut sites are removed during assembly, ligation can proceed immediately - no purification step.
steps.intro: Golden Gate uses Type IIS enzymes (which cut outside their recognition site) to create scarless, directional, one-tube assemblies of 10+ fragments. Because cut sites are removed during assembly, ligation can proceed immediately - no purification step.

instructions.title: Design overhangs
instructions.description: Place Type IIS sites so digestion leaves unique 4 nt overhangs that define fragment order.

instructions.title: Domesticate fragments
instructions.description: Remove internal recognition sites via silent mutations so only the designed sites are cut.

instructions.title: Cycle digest-ligate
instructions.description: Run alternating digest/ligation cycles in one tube, then transform.

submission.description: Assemble an ordered multi-part construct by Golden Gate and confirm correct assembly by screening.
